title: Monthly cost-support table (v1)
description:
One calendar month of the published cost-support table: what the movement's running costs were, who paid them, and what the fees account passed on to the listed recipients (ops decision D29 §3, as amended 2026-09-06 by D33 and D34).

ONE DOCUMENT PER CALENDAR MONTH, AND THE SHAPE IS IDENTICAL IN EVERY MONTH — that invariance is the contract. Supporters are ROWS, never schema constants: when a supporter stops, its row goes to zero and falls off, and no heading, no rule text and no published claim changes (D29 §3). An empty month is the same document with empty arrays, zero amounts and its notes — never a month left out, and never a zero dressed up as a result.

FOUR OUTGOING LINES AND NOTHING ELSE (D34 item 5; invariant I1): the direct invoices nobody supported, the reserve retention, the steward hardship pay, and one transfer per listed recipient. The fees account receives every Purpose Fee payout and nothing else; cost support NEVER passes through it (invariant I4) — a supporter settles a listed direct invoice IN PLACE OF the fees account, by name and amount, or the support did not happen (I5). The full bill is published even when support covers all of it (I6). No person other than the holder of the one essential operating role is ever paid from Purpose Fees, and only under the published hardship rule with its source declaration (I9, D34 item 3).

THE ARITHMETIC A READER CHECKS, stated here because JSON Schema cannot express a sum across items — the same treatment `purpose-yml.v1` gives its micro-share bound: (1) `chargedToFeesMinor` = max(0, `directCostsTotalMinor` − `supportTotalMinor` − `reserveAdvanceTotalMinor`) + `deferredChargesTotalMinor`, each of the two last members 0 where the document carries none; (2) `supportTotalMinor` + `reserveAdvanceTotalMinor` ≤ `directCostsTotalMinor` — whatever a supporter wants to give beyond the month's direct costs is that supporter's own donation, in its own name, and is not part of this model; (3) `passedOnMinor` = `purposeFeesNetMinor` − `chargedToFeesMinor` − `reserveRetentionMinor` (a document written before 2026-09-14 also subtracts `hardshipPayMinor`, a member struck on that date); (4) the `transfers[]` amounts sum to `passedOnMinor`; (5) `directCostsTotalMinor` is the sum of `directCosts[]`, `supportTotalMinor` the sum of `supporters[]`, `reserveAdvanceTotalMinor` the sum of `directCosts[].reserveAdvanceMinor` and `deferredChargesTotalMinor` the sum of `deferredCharges[]`. Every total is written rather than derived so a reader can check the arithmetic against the file it is published in.

A BILL THE RESERVE ADVANCES IS CHARGED ONCE (Calculation Rules Nr. 17; added 2026-10-01). When a close's Purpose Fees cannot carry a direct invoice, only its charge to the fees is deferred, and the invoice itself is paid when due: by the operations reserve as far as the reserve's opening balance for the month holds and statutes Art. 6g(3) allows, and by a named supporter for the rest. The month that pays it lists the invoice in full with its `reserveAdvanceMinor`, outside the charged line, and the reserve's `direct-cost-out` movement of that amount. The first close whose fees can bear the charge makes it, once and whole, as a `deferredCharges[]` line of the same amount, inside the charged line and the running year's total against the cap, and the reserve's `refill-from-fees` movement pays the reserve back. That close is normally a later month's, and it is the paying month's own where its close can carry the bill after all. Each movement names its invoice and the month of the advance (`invoiceRef`, `advancedIn`). The advance's movement is in the document that lists the advance, because an advanced invoice's `paidOn` is the day the reserve account books its payment. The refill is listed by the month the reserve account books it: the closing month itself where the fees account paid the reserve back before the close, and otherwise, like the retention, a later month, normally the next. The reserve's ordinary retention continues beside the refill until the target.

EVERY LINE CARRIES ITS EVIDENCE: the rail payout statement, the invoice, the supporter's payment, the bank line, each listed recipient's receipt (D29 §3, URS GOV-072). The proof is publication to the invoice, not a signature (D29 §8).

Money is integer minor units plus an ISO currency code, never a float; the period is one calendar month, the same unit as the sweep, and the annual report aggregates months without ever restating them. The cap and the retention limit are figures in the statutes' own text (Art. 6(3) and Art. 6g(2); ops decision D43 item 1), the reserve's target follows the rule of Art. 6g(1) (ops decision D114), and no cap is ever raised for a purchase already made (Art. 22(4); invariant I7). A closed month is never edited: a correction is a forward-dated `annotations[]` line, on the same never-restate doctrine as the ledger (FS07-042).

x-psn.phase: P-M3 (producer). At v0 the table is hand-maintained and no calendar month with a Purpose Fee payout has closed, so nothing is published yet and the page says so.
x-psn.artifactPath: no path in the FS-00 §6.2 catalogue yet — deliberately deferred; at v0 one hand-maintained file (`src/data/cost-support/index.json` in the website repo, one entry per closed month) rendered on the transparency page. The published per-month path is fixed when FS-00 §6.2 adopts this artifact.
x-psn.producer: v0: the operator, from the fees account's own statement and the invoices · P-M3: `jobs.ledger-publish`, beside the monthly ledger export
consumers: the annual transparency report, which aggregates months and never restates them
fsRefs: FS-07 amendment banner (D29 §3; D33; D34) — re-specified at P-M3 with cost-support.v1

month.description: The calendar month this table covers. The period is always one calendar month — the same unit as the sweep (D29 §2).

currency.description: Reporting currency (CHF). Every `*Minor` field in this document is in this currency.

closed.description: True once the month is closed and the table is final. An open month may still receive invoices and supporter payments; a CLOSED month is never edited — a correction is an `annotations[]` line (D29 §3, FS07-042).

financialYear.description: The financial year `yearRunningTotalMinor` accumulates over, when it is not read from `month`. The annual cap test is a test on this year (GOV-001).

purposeFeesNetMinor.description: F — the Purpose Fees the payment rail paid out to the Association in the month, NET of the rail's processing fee (D29 §2). The processing fee is published in the fee stack; it is not a cost of the Association and never appears in the cost line. Zero is a published state: a month with no payout.

directCosts.description: C, itemised — the month's direct costs, one entry per third-party invoice, complete even where a supporter settled all of it (invariant I6) or the operations reserve advanced it (`reserveAdvanceMinor`). A direct cost is a third-party invoice for a service that exists ONLY for the movement, billed to an account of the Association used only for the movement, in the eligible classes of the Cost Class Rules, the board rulebook under statutes Art. 22(7) (D29 §2.1; ops decision D43 item 1). It is never a bill that also serves another activity; a shared invoice is a direct cost only for the line items that serve the movement alone. Amended 2026-09-14 by the operator's override, written into the statutes set for adoption at the founding assembly of 1 October 2026: personnel cost IS now an eligible class inside C and inside the one running-cost cap, published as one line per function and never by name, and pay to a board member needs the prior minuted approval of at least two other board members with no interest of their own in any pay (statutes Art. 6f(3); ops decision D43 item 7). The former separate line `hardshipPayMinor` and the single essential operating role are struck.

directCostsTotalMinor.description: The sum of `directCosts[].amountMinor`. Written, not derived, so a reader can check `chargedToFeesMinor` against this file alone.

supporters.description: S, by supporter — the named supporters that settled listed direct invoices in place of the fees account this month (D29 §2, §3). Supporters are ROWS, never constants, and the list is DATA: no supporter's name appears in any statute, pledge, constant or fixed copy (invariant I8). A supporter is listed for the months in which it paid something and drops off when it stops; an empty array is a valid month, and the document's shape does not change.

supportTotalMinor.description: The sum of `supporters[].amountMinor`, and, with `reserveAdvanceTotalMinor`, never more than `directCostsTotalMinor` (D29 §2: support beyond the month's direct costs is the supporter's own donation, in its own name, outside this model).

reserveAdvanceTotalMinor.description: A — the sum of `directCosts[].reserveAdvanceMinor`: the part of the month's invoices the operations reserve advanced because the close's Purpose Fees could not carry them (Calculation Rules Nr. 17). Written, not derived, so a reader can check `chargedToFeesMinor` against this file alone. Required whenever an entry carries `reserveAdvanceMinor`; a document without one reads it as 0.

deferredCharges.description: D, itemised — the deferred charges this close makes: one line per invoice the operations reserve advanced, in this month or an earlier one, whose charge to the Purpose Fees is made here, once and whole, its money paid back to the reserve (Calculation Rules Nr. 17; statutes Art. 6a(3): a direct third-party invoice no supporter settled). Every line is inside `chargedToFeesMinor`, and so inside the running year's total against the cap, and is published in the month it is charged (statutes Art. 6(5)). The invoice itself stays, in full, on the table of the month that paid it: a deferred charge is never a second listing of its cost, and an advance is never charged twice. Absent or empty: the close makes none.

deferredChargesTotalMinor.description: The sum of `deferredCharges[].amountMinor`. Written, not derived, so a reader can check `chargedToFeesMinor` against this file alone. Required whenever `deferredCharges` is present; a document without it reads it as 0.

chargedToFeesMinor.description: max(0, `directCostsTotalMinor` − `supportTotalMinor` − `reserveAdvanceTotalMinor`) + `deferredChargesTotalMinor` — the direct invoices no supporter settled and the operations reserve did not advance, paid from the fees account, and the deferred charges this close makes for invoices the reserve advanced (each of the two last members 0 where the document carries none). There is NO percentage levy: this figure is a sum of itemised invoices, each linked to its evidence (D29 §2, ops decision D31 item 6; URS ENG-026).

yearRunningTotalMinor.description: The financial year's running total of charged-to-fees, including this month. The cap test is ANNUAL and is tested here, never on a month: a month may exceed the cap (an annual domain renewal lands in one month), the year may not, and whatever would exceed it for the year is not charged to Purpose Fees: it is paid from money of the Association that is not Purpose Fees (statutes Art. 6(4); GOV-001, invariant ENG-077). A deferred charge counts in the year of the close that makes it; an invoice the reserve advanced counts in no year until then, and never twice.

capBps.description: The annual cap on charged-to-fees, in basis points of the financial year's Purpose Fees net of the rail's processing fee. `null` until the number is set with counsel and written into the constitution — nothing renders a figure nobody has approved. The cap number is an open question of the record (URS §21 OPEN-05 owns it; 15% = 1500 bps, a figure in the statutes' own text (Art. 6(3); ops decision D43 item 1)) and it may only ever be lowered (invariant I7).

reserveRetentionMinor.description: R — what the month retained into the operations reserve (ops decision D34 item 4): at most a published share of the month's Purpose Fees until the reserve holds its published target, and nothing at all above target. Zero is a published state, and the line appears in EVERY month with its note. The reserve is an account that is not the fees account and is never a refund reserve.

reserveRetentionNote.description: Why the retention line reads what it reads — 'target reached', or the rule that produced the amount (D34 item 4, D29 §3). Required in every month, including a month that retained nothing: the rule applied and produced nothing is a published fact, not an absence.

hardshipPayMinor.description: STRUCK 2026-09-14 by the operator's override, written into the statutes set for adoption at the founding assembly of 1 October 2026: the steward hardship rule, its monthly ceiling, its share of trailing fees, its episode and the single essential operating role are gone. Personnel cost is now an ordinary direct-cost class inside the one running-cost cap (`chargedToFeesMinor`, `capBps`), published as one line per function. This member is retained in the published contract so that documents written before that date keep validating, and is no longer written. Its historical meaning follows. H — the steward hardship pay from Purpose Fees for the month, in total employer cost (ops decision D34 item 3). Paid to the holder of the one essential operating role and to nobody else, ever (invariant I9), and only when the earlier sources are exhausted: the other activity's published operating needs, then a listed supporter or sponsor, then the operations reserve, then Purpose Fees last of all. Two caps govern and the lower wins — a monthly ceiling in total employer cost, and a share of the trailing twelve months' Purpose Fees — both annex values, both able only to fall. Zero is a published state, and the line appears in EVERY month with its declaration.

hardshipSourceDeclaration.description: STRUCK 2026-09-14 by the operator's override, written into the statutes set for adoption at the founding assembly of 1 October 2026: the steward hardship rule, its monthly ceiling, its share of trailing fees, its episode and the single essential operating role are gone. Personnel cost is now an ordinary direct-cost class inside the one running-cost cap (`chargedToFeesMinor`, `capBps`), published as one line per function. This member is retained in the published contract so that documents written before that date keep validating, and is no longer written. Its historical meaning follows. The month's source declaration (D34 items 2 and 3(a), 3(d)): which of the sources were exhausted, or that the rule was not activated because the earlier sources sufficed. Required in every month — the declaration is the published proof that Purpose Fees were the last source, so its absence in a zero month would remove exactly the fact a reader came for.

hardshipApprovalRef.description: STRUCK 2026-09-14 by the operator's override, written into the statutes set for adoption at the founding assembly of 1 October 2026: the steward hardship rule, its monthly ceiling, its share of trailing fees, its episode and the single essential operating role are gone. Personnel cost is now an ordinary direct-cost class inside the one running-cost cap (`chargedToFeesMinor`, `capBps`), published as one line per function. This member is retained in the published contract so that documents written before that date keep validating, and is no longer written. Its historical meaning follows. The reference of the monthly approval by the board members other than the holder, the holder abstaining (D34 item 3(c), Art. 68 ZGB) — minuted and published. Required whenever `hardshipPayMinor` is above zero.

hardshipEpisodeMonth.description: STRUCK 2026-09-14 by the operator's override, written into the statutes set for adoption at the founding assembly of 1 October 2026: the steward hardship rule, its monthly ceiling, its share of trailing fees, its episode and the single essential operating role are gone. Personnel cost is now an ordinary direct-cost class inside the one running-cost cap (`chargedToFeesMinor`, `capBps`), published as one line per function. This member is retained in the published contract so that documents written before that date keep validating, and is no longer written. Its historical meaning follows. Which month of the current hardship episode this is (D34 item 3(e)): an episode lasts at most twelve months and is renewed only by a members' vote. The published episode length travels on the ledger export's `policy.hardshipEpisodeMonths`; this field is the position inside the episode. Required whenever `hardshipPayMinor` is above zero.

passedOnMinor.description: What the fees account passes on for the month: `purposeFeesNetMinor` − `chargedToFeesMinor` − `reserveRetentionMinor` (a document written before 2026-09-14 also subtracts `hardshipPayMinor`, a member struck on that date). It goes DIRECTLY to the organisations on the published Recipient List, in the shares the published allocation rule produces — no intermediary, no pooled vehicle, no earmark and no handling fee (ops decision D33 item 1). The `transfers[]` rows sum to this figure.

transfers.description: One row per listed recipient, never one row per category fund (ops decision D33 item 1): for every category the month's allocation gave an amount to, there is one row for each ACTIVE listed recipient of that category, in the shares the published list's `shareRule` produces. A category the allocation gave nothing to has no rows at all. Under the lock-before-sweep rule the month's allocation is computed at the lock, which comes before the transfer (statutes Art. 6a(4); D109 item 4), and each recipient's share is transferred directly from the fees account within the deadline of statutes Art. 6a(4), counted from the credit of the month's earliest rail payout (D33 item 4; D43 item 4: every payout has its own deadline). Every share is transferred in the month it is allocated however small: there is no roll-forward at any granularity and no minimum-wire threshold (D33 item 5). A row published between the lock and the sweep carries `status: "scheduled"` — a scheduled share is not a transfer, and this contract will not let one be rendered as though it were.

reserve.description: The operations reserve's memo line (ops decision D34 item 4): movements, balance and target are published monthly. The reserve sits in an account that is NOT the fees account, is spent only on direct costs that are not charged to Purpose Fees because of the cap (personnel included; statutes Art. 6g(3)) and on the transfer charges of the final sweep, and is never a refund reserve. Under Calculation Rules Nr. 17 it also advances, as far as statutes Art. 6g(3) allows, a direct invoice whose charge a close's Purpose Fees cannot carry, and the close that later charges it pays the reserve back (`direct-cost-out`, `refill-from-fees`). Amended 2026-09-14: the essential operating role and the hardship rule are struck.

balanceMinor.description: The reserve's balance at the end of the month.

targetMinor.description: The published target, set by the rule of statutes Art. 6g(1) as amended by ops decision D114 (2026-10-05): half of the direct costs under Art. 6 (the personnel costs under Art. 6f included) of the Purpose Source activity in the previous financial year, whatever funds paid them — Purpose Fees, cost support, the operations reserve or free funds — annualised where that financial year was shorter than twelve months. The board sets it each January from the published monthly tables and publishes it; in the first financial year it uses the direct costs incurred since founding, annualised. It replaces the fixed CHF 27,000 of ops decision D43 item 1. `null` on a table for a month before the statutes were adopted; nothing renders a figure nobody has approved.

note.description: The month's reserve narrative: the movements, or that the account holds nothing yet.

movements.description: The month's movements in and out of the reserve, published one by one (D34 item 4). Inflows from a sponsor, from another activity's profit and from other unrestricted income are movements of this account, never rows of the fees account.

allOf.$comment: Added 2026-10-01 (Calculation Rules Nr. 17): the reserve's payment of an advanced invoice and its refill each name the advance they belong to, and no other movement names one.

amountMinor.description: Positive into the reserve, negative out of it.

kind.description: `retention-from-fees` is the D34 item 4 retention (and equals this month's `reserveRetentionMinor` when it is the only one). `unrestricted-income` is a sponsor, another activity's profit or other unrestricted income — the failsafe does not depend on any one of them. `direct-cost-out` is the reserve paying a direct invoice it advances (Calculation Rules Nr. 17), of exactly that invoice's `reserveAdvanceMinor`, on its `paidOn`. `refill-from-fees` is the fees account paying the reserve back the deferred charge a close made, of exactly that charge's `amountMinor`, in the month the reserve account books it: the closing month or a later one. Both name the advance (`invoiceRef`, `advancedIn`). The two `-out` kinds are the only permitted spends.

invoiceRef.description: On a `direct-cost-out` or `refill-from-fees` movement, and on no other: the invoice the reserve paid in advance or was paid back for, by its reference.

advancedIn.description: On a `direct-cost-out` or `refill-from-fees` movement, and on no other: the month whose table lists the invoice in full with its `reserveAdvanceMinor`. With `invoiceRef` it names the advance the movement belongs to.

sponsorshipId.description: On an `unrestricted-income` movement paid from a sponsorship’s unused balance (D44), the id of that sponsorship in the published sponsor register.

recipientListVersion.description: The version of the Recipient List in force for the month (`recipient-list.v1`), published so a reader can resolve every `recipientId` in `transfers[]` against the list that governed the transfer (URS TRN-024 as amended). Absent while no list has been adopted — and no transfer is made before an adopted list is published.

evidence.description: The month's own evidence — above all the rail payout statement behind `purposeFeesNetMinor` (D29 §3). An EMPTY array is a valid month: a month with no payout has no statement, and an empty month is the same document rather than a missing one.

annotations.description: Forward-only narrative context. A closed month is never edited and never restated: a correction is a new annotation here, or a new month's entry, exactly as a ledger correction is a forward-dated row (FS07-042, D29 §3).

methodologyUrl.description: The published methodology: the eligible direct-cost classes and the annual cap; what cost support is and why it never enters the fees account; the two capped lines of D34; the lock-before-sweep rule; and the never-restate doctrine.

allOf.$comment: Historical only — the rule was struck 2026-09-14 and no document written after that date carries `hardshipPayMinor`. For documents that do: D34 item 3(c) and 3(e), pay above zero exists only with the month’s approval by the members other than the holder, inside a numbered episode of at most twelve months.
Added 2026-10-01 (Calculation Rules Nr. 17): the advances' total is written whenever an invoice carries an advance, so a reader can always check `chargedToFeesMinor` against the file.
Added 2026-10-01 (Calculation Rules Nr. 17): the deferred charges' total is written whenever the document lists them.

invoiceRef.description: The invoice's own reference. One entry per invoice: the cost line is itemised to the invoice, never summarised into a rate.

description.description: What the invoice was for, in the words a reader can match to the class.

amountMinor.description: The invoice amount in the document's currency. An invoice is a positive amount; a credit note is its own forward entry, never an edit.

supporter.description: The named supporter that settled THIS invoice in place of the fees account (D29 §2, invariant I5). Absent means the fees account paid it, so the invoice sits inside `chargedToFeesMinor` — unless `reserveAdvanceMinor` says the operations reserve advanced it. With both, the supporter settled the part the reserve did not advance, and its `supporters[]` line carries that part for this invoice. Support never passes through the fees account (I4), and undisclosed support is the one thing this model forbids — it is the only thing that could make the published cost line flatter than the truth.

paidOn.description: When the invoice was actually paid. Charged-to-fees for a period is what the account paid in that period: an invoice for an earlier month paid late is charged in the period it is paid (D31 item 2), and the annual cap test is unaffected. For an invoice the operations reserve advanced, the day the reserve account's statement books its payment, which is its `direct-cost-out` movement's date.

reserveAdvanceMinor.description: Advanced by the reserve: the part of THIS invoice the operations reserve paid when it fell due, because the close's Purpose Fees could not carry it (Calculation Rules Nr. 17), at most the invoice's `amountMinor`. It is not charged to fees in this month (it is subtracted as `reserveAdvanceTotalMinor`). The first close that can bear it charges it once, whole, as a `deferredCharges[]` line of the same amount, and this document lists the reserve's `direct-cost-out` movement of the same amount, naming this invoice and this month. The rest of the invoice, if any, is the named supporter's (`supporter`). Absent: the reserve advanced nothing.

evidence.description: At least the invoice; and where a supporter settled it, the supporter's payment as well.

directCostClass.description: The eligible direct-cost classes of the Cost Class Rules, the board rulebook under statutes Art. 22(7) (D29 §2.1, in order; ops decision D43 item 1): the movement's own domains and marks; DNS, hosting, CDN, edge compute and storage for the movement's own properties on the movement's own accounts; transactional email for them; monitoring, error tracking and the status page for them; payment-rail charges not already netted from the payout; `transfer-charges` — the bank-transfer and currency-conversion charges on the outbound transfers to the listed recipients, one entry per transfer (ops decision D33 item 5); and the fee of a review engagement scoped SOLELY to the fees account and the routing. The *kind* rule is constitutional; the list itself is board-amendable with publication, so this enum may gain a class additively. Never eligible, by construction: bookkeeping, counsel, the Association's own filings, insurance, any person's salary, honorarium, expense claim or contractor invoice, anything used by a person, and anything on an account that also serves another activity.

name.description: The supporter's name: another activity of the Association, a member, an outside sponsor or a future project. Names are data and appear only here and on the rendered table.

amountMinor.description: What this supporter settled in the month. Zero is representable — the row a supporter's last month leaves behind before it falls off the list — and changes nothing about the document's shape.

invoiceRefs.description: The `directCosts[].invoiceRef` values this supporter settled, so support is checkable invoice by invoice rather than in aggregate.

evidence.description: The supporter's own payment. Support is listed with its evidence or it did not happen (invariant I5).

sponsorshipId.description: When this support was paid from a sponsorship (ops decision D44): the id of that sponsorship in the published sponsor register (`sponsorship.v1`, `/sponsors.json`), so a reader can follow a named supporter line back to the invoice it came from. The supporter `name` is then the sponsor’s name exactly as the register prints it.

deferredCharge.description: Deferred charge: one invoice the operations reserve advanced, charged to the Purpose Fees by this close, once and whole, its money paid back to the reserve (Calculation Rules Nr. 17). Published in the month it is charged, with a reference to its evidence (statutes Art. 6(5)), it becomes one `charged-to-fees` row, as every charged invoice does (FS07-021). It carries no day of its own: the close makes the charge, and the reserve's `refill-from-fees` movement is listed by the month the reserve account books it.

invoiceRef.description: The invoice's own reference, as the table of the month that advanced it carries it.

advancedIn.description: The month whose table lists the invoice in full with its `reserveAdvanceMinor`: this document's month, or an earlier one.

amountMinor.description: The deferred charge: exactly the invoice's `reserveAdvanceMinor`, which is less than its full amount where a supporter settled the rest. A charge is never split across closes.

description.description: What the invoice was for, as on the table of the month that advanced it.

evidence.description: At least the invoice, as the table of the month that advanced it refers to it.

supplier.description: Who sent the invoice (ops decision D79 items 4.3 and 4.4; added 2026-10-01). A company is published by its legal name. A natural person, sole traders included, is never named: only by the role they served in, which is a function, never a name, an address or another detail that identifies them.

kind.description: `company`: a legal entity, published by its legal name. `natural-person`: a person, sole traders included, published by role only.

legalName.description: A company's legal name, as its register entry or its invoice states it. Only on `company`.

role.description: A natural person's role, for example "independent reviewer of the fees account". Only on `natural-person`, and never the person's name.

recipientId.description: The listed recipient this share belongs to, resolvable against the Recipient List version named in `recipientListVersion` (`recipient-list.v1`). Money rows name organisations on the published list, never persons (URS ENG-083).

category.description: The recipient's category, from the movement's seven published categories. The closed menu is published once in `category-menu.v1` (`$defs.slug`); this contract set may not `$ref` across files — each schema must validate on its own after a single download — so every other field carrying the vocabulary constrains it by pattern and names the published menu, as `ledger-row.v1.categoryFundId` does, or carries a copy of the enum that `check:menu` holds identical to it.

amountMinor.description: This recipient's share of `passedOnMinor` for the month.

status.description: `scheduled` between the lock and the sweep: the share is computed and published, and the money has not moved. `transferred` once it has, with its date and receipt. The distinction is the honesty rule in the contract itself — a scheduled share is never rendered as a transfer, and no impact figure exists before a real transfer row.

date.description: The transfer's value date. Required once `status` is `transferred`.

receiptRef.description: The recipient's receipt for this transfer (D33 item 2(f)). Required once `status` is `transferred`.

endToEndId.description: The credit transfer's end-to-end identifier, so a bank line and a published row can be matched by anyone holding both (ops decision D33 item 4). Since 1.3.0 it is `psn-YYYYMM-` and the last 12 characters of the recipient's ULID, 23 characters: ISO 20022 types `EndToEndId` as Max35Text, which the earlier form `psn-{month}-{recipientId}` (42 characters) exceeded (ops FS07-062, ruling of 2026-10-07). The earlier form stays valid for rows written before it.

note.description: Narrative for this row — for instance that a recipient removed for cause mid-month has no row and its share went to the other recipients of its category (D33 item 3).

evidence.description: The bank line and the recipient's receipt. Required once `status` is `transferred`: a transfer nobody can check is not a published transfer.

allOf.$comment: A transfer nobody can check is not a published transfer: the evidence array must be non-empty, not merely present. The sibling definitions carry the same minItems 1 on their own evidence.

evidenceLink.description: One piece of evidence behind one line. Every line of this table carries at least one (D29 §3, URS GOV-072).

kind.description: The classes of evidence the record names for this table: the rail payout statement, the invoice, the supporter's payment, the bank line, each listed recipient's receipt (D29 §3), the reserve's published movements (D34 item 4) and the minuted monthly approval of a hardship payment (D34 item 3(c)).

ref.description: The evidence's own reference — invoice number, statement line, payout id, receipt number, minute number. A reference a reader can ask for by name, present even where the document itself is not published in full.

url.description: Where the document is published, when it is. Absent is honest: not every piece of evidence is a public URL, and a missing link must not be indistinguishable from a missing document.
